claim: ERL1-YFP marks the plasma membrane of stomatal-lineage cells, most notably late meristemoids.
source: As reported previously (Qi et al., 2017), a functional ERL1-YFP fusion protein driven by its endogenous promoter (ERL1pro::ERL1-YFP) in erl1 seedlings marks the plasma membrane of stomatal-lineage cells, most notably late meristemoids.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Qi et al., 2017) and by the experimental observation described in the text.

claim: ERL1-YFP punctae co-localize with FM4-64, a styryl dye used to trace endocytic pathways in plants.
source: In addition, we detected some punctae highlighted by ERL1-YFP that co-localized with FM4-64, a styryl dye used to trace the endocytic pathways in plants (Meckel et al., 2004; Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation (Meckel et al., 2004), by the experimental observation in the text, and by reference to Figure 1A showing co-localization.

claim: ERL1-YFP extensively co-localizes and moves together with RFP-ARA7.
source: ERL1-YFP extensively co-localizes and moves together with RFP-ARA7 (Figure 1B,C, Video 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, 1C, and Video 1.

claim: Only 25% of ERL1-YFP-positive punctae are labelled by SYP43-RFP.
source: whereas only 25% and 18% of ERL1-YFP-positive punctae are also labelled by SYP43-RFP and SYP22-RFP, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from co-localization analysis.

claim: Only 18% of ERL1-YFP-positive punctae are labelled by SYP22-RFP.
source: whereas only 25% and 18% of ERL1-YFP-positive punctae are also labelled by SYP43-RFP and SYP22-RFP, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from co-localization analysis.

claim: ERL1-YFP predominantly resides on the MVB/LE.
source: Thus, ERL1-YFP predominantly resides on the MVB/LE.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the co-localization data with RFP-ARA7 and the limited co-localization with other markers.

claim: Wortmannin application on Arabidopsis seedlings results in the formation of typical ring-like Wm bodies marked by both ERL1-YFP and RFP-ARA7.
source: The Wm application on Arabidopsis seedlings resulted in the formation of typical ring-like Wm bodies marked by both ERL1-YFP and RFP-ARA7 (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Wm bodies are much larger (average size of 0.993 ± 0.203 μm) than the endosomes (average size of 0.383 ± 0.063 μm).
source: These Wm bodies are much larger (average size of 0.993 ± 0.203 μm) than the endosomes (average size of 0.383 ± 0.063 μm), thus easy to recognize and quantify (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Wortmannin is a fungal drug that can cause fusion of MVB/LEs by inhibiting phosphatidylinositol-3 (PI3) and phosphatidylinositol-4 (PI4) kinases.
source: This is further confirmed by a pharmacological approach using Wortmannin (Wm), a fungal drug that can cause fusion of MVB/LEs by inhibiting phosphatidylinositol-3 (PI3) and phosphatidylinositol-4 (PI4) kinases (Foissner et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Foissner et al., 2016 and established knowledge about Wortmannin's mechanism of action.

claim: Concanamycin A treatment following the wash-out of the endocytic tracer dye FM4-64 led to accumulation of strong vacuolar YFP signals surrounded by an FM4-64 stained tonoplast.
source: As shown in Figure 2, Concanamycin A treatment following the wash-out of the endocytic tracer dye FM4-64 led to accumulation of strong vacuolar YFP signals surrounded by an FM4-64 stained tonoplast.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Concanamycin A is a specific inhibitor of vacuolar H+-ATPase that is known to reduce protein degradation in the lytic vacuole.
source: Because we did not observe clear accumulation of ERL1 in a vacuole, and co-localization of SYP22-RFP and ERL1-YFP was limited to the endosomes (Figure 1B,C), we took a pharmacological approach using Concanamycin A, a specific inhibitor of vacuolar H+-ATPase that is known to reduce protein degradation in the lytic vacuole (Kleine-Vehn et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kleine-Vehn et al., 2008 and established knowledge about Concanamycin A's mechanism of action.

claim: Within the stomatal precursor cells, ERL1 undergoes endocytic trafficking from the plasma membrane to MVB/LE and is destined to vacuolar degradation.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that, within the stomatal precursor cells, ERL1 undergoes endocytic trafficking from the plasma membrane to MVB/LE and is destined to vacuolar degradation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined cell biological, pharmacological, and biochemical analyses presented in the text.

claim: BFA treatment in roots results in formation of characteristic BFA bodies, which are conglomerates of TGN surrounded by the Golgi apparatus.
source: BFA, a chemical inhibitor of ADP-ribosylation factor guanine-nucleotide exchange factors (ARF-GEFs) including GNOM has been widely used to block endosomal recycling and endocytosis of membrane proteins (Geldner et al., 2003). BFA treatment in roots results in formation of characteristic BFA bodies, which are conglomerates of TGN surrounded by the Golgi apparatus (Geldner et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Geldner et al., 2003 and established knowledge about BFA effects in roots.

claim: BFA application to Arabidopsis leaves triggers re-absorption of Golgi membrane collapsed onto the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: It has been reported, however, that BFA application to Arabidopsis leaves triggers re-absorption of Golgi membrane collapsed onto the endoplasmic reticulum (Robinson et al., 2008; Langhans et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Robinson et al., 2008 and Langhans et al., 2011.

claim: Low BFA concentration at 30 μM does not confer any discernable effects on the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: Low BFA concentration at 30 μM does not confer any discernable effects on the endoplasmic reticulum (GFP-HDEL; Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Under 30 μM BFA treatment, BFA bodies are surrounded by ST-YFP, exhibiting characteristic membrane organization of BFA bodies reported in roots.
source: Under this condition, BFA bodies (magenta arrows) are surrounded by ST-YFP (green arrows, Figure 3C), exhibiting characteristic membrane organization of BFA bodies reported in roots (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: BFA at very high concentration, 180 μM, conferred aberrant spherical structures of the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: In contrast, BFA at very high concentration, 180 μM, conferred aberrant spherical structures of the endoplasmic reticulum (Figure 3A,B), which was also previously reported (Nakano et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B, and by citation to Nakano et al., 2009.

claim: At 180 μM BFA treatment, Golgi absorbed ER, which confers ring-like structure of membrane accumulating ST-YFP.
source: Indeed, at 180 μM BFA treatment, we observed Golgi absorbed ER, which confers ring-like structure of membrane accumulating ST-YFP (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Previously reported effects of BFA on leaves were observed only when extremely high concentration of BFA was applied.
source: These results demonstrate that previously reported effects of BFA on leaves were observed only when extremely high concentration of BFA was applied.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data comparing different BFA concentrations.

claim: All marker lines show the formation of characteristic BFA bodies in meristemoids, without discernible collapse of Golgi apparatus into the endoplasmic reticulum when treated with 30 μM BFA.
source: All marker lines show the formation of characteristic BFA bodies in meristemoids, without discernible collapse of Golgi apparatus into the endoplasmic reticulum (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 30 μM BFA confers BFA body formation just like when applied to roots.
source: Taken together, our extensive documentation shows that 30 μM BFA confers BFA body formation just like when applied to roots.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the extensive documentation of BFA effects at different concentrations.

claim: BFA can be used to study the endocytosis of ERL1 in meristemoids.
source: Therefore, BFA can be used to study the endocytosis of ERL1 in meristemoids.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the demonstration that 30 μM BFA confers BFA body formation in meristemoids without aberrant effects.

claim: ERL1 forms a heterodimer with TMM to create a pocket for the proper binding of its major ligand EPF1.
source: A previous work has shown that ERL1 forms a heterodimer with TMM, a receptor protein, to create a pocket for the proper binding of its major ligand EPF1 (Lee et al., 2012; Lin et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2012 and Lin et al., 2017.

claim: The absence of TMM results in clustered stomata.
source: The absence of TMM results in clustered stomata (Figure 4A), indicating that TMM is required for EPF1-ERL1 signaling to enforce proper stomatal spacing (Hara et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and by citations to Hara et al., 2007 and Lee et al., 2012.

claim: TMM is required for EPF1-ERL1 signaling to enforce proper stomatal spacing.
source: The absence of TMM results in clustered stomata (Figure 4A), indicating that TMM is required for EPF1-ERL1 signaling to enforce proper stomatal spacing (Hara et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by the observation of clustered stomata in tmm mutants and by citations to Hara et al., 2007 and Lee et al., 2012.

claim: The number of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes per meristemoid cell was reduced in tmm.
source: The number of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes per meristemoid cell was reduced in tmm (Figure 4B; p=1.58e-14, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, with statistical significance.

claim: Fluorescent volume intensity (voxel) ratio analysis revealed statistically-significant reduction of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes in tmm.
source: Fluorescent volume intensity (voxel) ratio analysis also revealed statistically-significant reduction of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes in tmm (Figure 4D, p=0.0049)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4D with statistical significance.

claim: There was significant reduction of ERL1-YFP-positive BFA bodies in 30 µM BFA-treated tmm compared to those in wild type.
source: Fluorescent volume intensity (voxel) ratio analysis also revealed statistically-significant reduction of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes in tmm (Figure 4D, p=0.0049) as well as significant reduction of ERL1-YFP-positive BFA bodies in 30 µM BFA-treated tmm (Figure 4D, p=4.64e-11) compared to those in wild type.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4D with statistical significance.

claim: Treatment with 50 µM CHX for 1 hr followed by either mock or 30 µM BFA led to reduction in the number of ERL1-YFP-positive BFA bodies in tmm mutant.
source: Treatment with 50 µM CHX for 1 hr followed by either mock or 30 µM BFA led to reduction in the number of ERL1-YFP-positive BFA bodies in tmm mutant (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, p=0.0154).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 with statistical significance.

claim: ERL1-YFP-positive BFA bodies are reduced in tmm mutant regardless of the presence or absence of CHX.
source: Thus, ERL1-YFP-positive BFA bodies are reduced in tmm mutant regardless of the presence or absence of CHX, thereby suggesting that the absence of TMM does not impact the ERL1 secretory pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduction of BFA bodies in tmm with and without CHX treatment.

claim: The absence of TMM does not impact the ERL1 secretory pathway.
source: Thus, ERL1-YFP-positive BFA bodies are reduced in tmm mutant regardless of the presence or absence of CHX, thereby suggesting that the absence of TMM does not impact the ERL1 secretory pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that CHX treatment does not change the reduction of BFA bodies in tmm.

claim: Wm treatment conferred significant reduction of ERL1-YFP-labelled Wm-bodies in tmm compared to that in wild type.
source: Next, we treated the seedlings with Wm, which conferred significant reduction of ERL1-YFP-labelled Wm-bodies in tmm compared to that in wild type (Figure 4E,F, p=1.40e-5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and 4F with statistical significance.

claim: TMM is critical for the endocytosis/internalization of ERL1 to MVB/LE.
source: Combined, the results suggest that TMM is critical for the endocytosis/internalization of ERL1 to MVB/LE.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of BFA and Wm treatments showing reduced ERL1 internalization in tmm mutants.

claim: EPF1 is the major ligand for ERL1.
source: Of the 11 EPF family members, EPF1 is the major ligand for ERL1 (Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2012.

claim: EPF1 signaling plays a negative role in stomatal development.
source: EPF1 signaling plays a negative role in stomatal development, and the induction of EPF1 peptide (iEPF1) confers arrested stomatal precursors (Figure 5A; Hara et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2012; Qi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and by citations to Hara et al., 2007, Lee et al., 2012, and Qi et al., 2017.

claim: The induction of EPF1 peptide (iEPF1) confers arrested stomatal precursors.
source: EPF1 signaling plays a negative role in stomatal development, and the induction of EPF1 peptide (iEPF1) confers arrested stomatal precursors (Figure 5A; Hara et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2012; Qi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and by citations to Hara et al., 2007, Lee et al., 2012, and Qi et al., 2017.

claim: Both plasma membrane and highly mobile endosomes are highlighted by ERL1-YFP in epf1.
source: As shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, both plasma membrane and highly mobile endosomes are highlighted by ERL1-YFP in epf1.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When treated with BFA or Wm, the number of ERL1-YFP-positive BFA or Wm bodies per cell are similar between wild type and epf1.
source: When treated with BFA or Wm, the number of ERL1-YFP-positive BFA or Wm bodies per cell are similar between wild type and epf1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–E, p=0.512 and p=0.647 for BFA and Wm treatment, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–E with statistical analysis.

claim: Although EPF1 is a primary ligand for ERL1, ERL1-YFP endocytosis is not severely affected in the absence of EPF1.
source: Therefore, although EPF1 is a primary ligand for ERL1, ERL1-YFP endocytosis is not severely affected in the absence of EPF1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that BFA and Wm treatments produce similar numbers of bodies in wild type and epf1.

claim: The number of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes per cell increases as the MEPF1 peptide concentration increases.
source: The number of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes per cell increases as the peptide concentration increases (Pearson correlation coefficient, r = 0.56, p=2.2 e-16; Figure 5C,E)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and 5E with statistical analysis showing correlation.

claim: MEPF1 peptide triggers the internalization of ERL1 in a dosage-dependent manner.
source: The number of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes per cell increases as the peptide concentration increases (Pearson correlation coefficient, r = 0.56, p=2.2 e-16; Figure 5C,E), indicating that MEPF1 peptide triggers the internalization of ERL1 in a dosage-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between MEPF1 concentration and number of endosomes.

claim: In the absence of TMM, the number of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes per cell remains low regardless of the MEPF1 dosage applied.
source: In the tmm background, however, the number of ERL1-YFP-positive endosomes per cell remains low regardless of the MEPF1 dosage applied (Figure 5D,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and 5F.

claim: In the absence of TMM, ERL1-YFP endocytosis is insensitive to MEPF1 application.
source: Thus, in the absence of TMM, ERL1-YFP endocytosis is insensitive to MEPF1 application, consistent with the genetic evidence that the tmm mutation is epistatic to induced EPF1 overexpression (iEPF1) (Hara et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2012; Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D, 5F, and 5B, and by citations to Hara et al., 2007 and Lee et al., 2012.

claim: The tmm mutation is epistatic to induced EPF1 overexpression (iEPF1).
source: Thus, in the absence of TMM, ERL1-YFP endocytosis is insensitive to MEPF1 application, consistent with the genetic evidence that the tmm mutation is epistatic to induced EPF1 overexpression (iEPF1) (Hara et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2012; Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hara et al., 2007 and Lee et al., 2012, and by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: EPF1 peptide ligand perception triggers the internalization of ERL1 receptor in a TMM-dependent manner.
source: Taken together, we conclude that EPF1 peptide ligand perception triggers the internalization of ERL1 receptor in a TMM-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results showing that MEPF1 triggers ERL1 internalization in wild type but not in tmm mutants.

claim: Binding of EPF1 to the ERL1-TMM receptor complex does not lead to conformational change.
source: A previous structural analysis has shown that binding of EPF1 to the ERL1-TMM receptor complex does not lead to conformational change (Lin et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2017.

claim: EPFL6 is normally expressed in the internal tissues of hypocotyls and stems, but not in the stomatal-lineage cells.
source: EPFL6 is normally expressed in the internal tissues of hypocotyls and stems, but not in the stomatal-lineage cells.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about EPFL6 expression pattern.

claim: Unlike EPF1, ectopic EPFL6 is a potent inhibitor of stomatal development even in the tmm mutant background.
source: Unlike EPF1, ectopic EPFL6 is a potent inhibitor of stomatal development even in the tmm mutant background (Abrash and Bergmann, 2010; Abrash et al., 2011; Uchida et al., 2012; Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Abrash and Bergmann, 2010, Abrash et al., 2011, and Uchida et al., 2012, and by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: The inhibition of stomatal formation by MEPFL6 is more sensitive in tmm mutant than in wild type.
source: Indeed, the inhibition of stomatal formation by MEPFL6 is more sensitive in tmm mutant than in wild type (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: MEPFL6 application induced ERL1-YFP internalization in a dosage-dependent manner regardless of the presence or absence of TMM.
source: In contrast to MEPF1, MEPFL6 application induced ERL1-YFP internalization in a dosage-dependent manner regardless of the presence or absence of TMM (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C–F.

claim: TMM is not required for EPFL6-triggered ERL1-YFP internalization.
source: The results indicate that TMM is not required for EPFL6-triggered ERL1-YFP internalization.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that MEPFL6 induces ERL1 internalization in both wild type and tmm mutants.

claim: The ERL1-YFP endocytosis accurately reflects the activity of ERL1 signaling to inhibit stomatal development.
source: Rather, the ERL1-YFP endocytosis accurately reflects the activity of ERL1 signaling to inhibit stomatal development (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between ERL1 endocytosis and stomatal development phenotypes shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Distinct EPF/EPFL peptide ligands activate a sub-population of ERL1 receptor complexes to internalize through a TMM-based discriminatory mechanism.
source: thereby supporting the notion that distinct EPF/EPFL peptide ligands activate a sub-population of ERL1 receptor complexes to internalize through a TMM-based discriminatory mechanism.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential requirements for TMM in EPF1- versus EPFL6-triggered ERL1 internalization.

claim: Stomagen promotes stomatal development by competing with other EPFs for binding to the same receptor complex, including ERL1.
source: Stomagen promotes stomatal development by competing with other EPFs for binding to the same receptor complex, including ERL1 (Figure 7A; Kondo et al., 2010; Sugano et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2017; Qi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kondo et al., 2010, Sugano et al., 2010, Lee et al., 2015, Lin et al., 2017, and Qi et al., 2017, and by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Unlike in mock-treated samples, YFP signal was detected inside the cells when bioactive Stomagen peptide was applied on seedlings expressing ERL1pro::ERL1-YFP in erl1.
source: For this purpose, we first applied bioactive Stomagen peptide on seedlings expressing ERL1pro::ERL1-YFP in erl1. Unlike in mock-treated samples, YFP signal was detected inside the cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Strong ERL1-YFP signals were detected in a ring-like structure surrounding the nucleus when Stomagen peptides were applied to ERL1-YFP in the erecta erl1 erl2 triple mutant background.
source: We subsequently treated Stomagen peptides to ERL1-YFP in the erecta erl1 erl2 triple mutant background to remove any potential redundancy among the three ERECTA-family receptors. Strikingly, strong ERL1-YFP signals were detected in a ring-like structure surrounding the nucleus (Figure 7B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The ring-like structure of ERL1-YFP co-localizes with the endoplasmic reticulum marker protein RFP-KDEL.
source: Strikingly, strong ERL1-YFP signals were detected in a ring-like structure surrounding the nucleus (Figure 7B), which co-localizes with the endoplasmic reticulum marker protein RFP-KDEL (Faraco et al., 2017; Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B and by citation to Faraco et al., 2017.

claim: Very faint ring-like structures were highlighted by ERL1-YFP in both mock and Stomagen-treated meristemoids in tmm seedlings expressing ERL1pro::ERL1-YFP.
source: Next, to reveal a consequence of inactive ERL1 receptor on its subcellular dynamics, we applied Stomagen peptide on tmm seedlings expressing ERL1pro::ERL1-YFP and carefully reexamined the signal. Very faint ring-like structures were highlighted by ERL1-YFP in both mock and Stomagen-treated meristemoids (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The faint ring-like structures of ERL1-YFP were enhanced in the erecta erl1 erl2 tmm quadruple mutant.
source: This was enhanced in the erecta erl1 erl2 tmm quadruple mutant (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: ERL1-YFP signals co-localized with Rhodamine B hexyl esters, a dye that stains the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: These ERL1-YFP signals co-localized with Rhodamine B hexyl esters, a dye that stains the endoplasmic reticulum (Hawes et al., 2018), suggesting that the absence of TMM intensifies accumulation of ERL1 in the endoplasmic reticulum (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C and by citation to Hawes et al., 2018.

claim: The absence of TMM intensifies accumulation of ERL1 in the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: These ERL1-YFP signals co-localized with Rhodamine B hexyl esters, a dye that stains the endoplasmic reticulum (Hawes et al., 2018), suggesting that the absence of TMM intensifies accumulation of ERL1 in the endoplasmic reticulum (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the co-localization of ERL1-YFP with ER marker in tmm mutants.

claim: Application of Stomagen peptide did not influence plasma membrane localization of BRI1-GFP.
source: Strong BRI1-GFP signals are detected at the plasma membrane of stomatal meristemoids, guard cells, as well as pavement cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2). Application of Stomagen peptide did not influence plasma membrane localization of BRI1-GFP (Figure 7—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The endoplasmic reticulum accumulation of ERL1-YFP upon Stomagen perception is not a universal phenomenon to LRR-RLKs.
source: thus the endoplasmic reticulum accumulation of ERL1-YFP upon Stomagen perception is not a universal phenomenon to LRR-RLKs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Stomagen does not affect BRI1-GFP localization.

claim: Endo-H cleaves N-glycans of proteins specifically in the endoplasmic reticulum, including LRR-RLKs.
source: Endo-H cleaves N-glycans of proteins specifically in the endoplasmic reticulum, including LRR-RLKs (Jin et al., 2007; Nekrasov et al., 2009), but not the remodeled glycan chains of proteins transported to the Golgi or further.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jin et al., 2007 and Nekrasov et al., 2009, and by established knowledge about Endo-H specificity.

claim: Under normal conditions, ERL1-FLAG is detected as a single band on immunoblots.
source: Under normal conditions, ERL1-FLAG is detected as a single band on immunoblots (Figure 7D, black arrow).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Endo-H digestion resulted in a faster mobility of ERL1-FLAG protein with at least three different sizes, suggestive of heterogeneous glycans.
source: The Endo-H digestion resulted in a faster mobility of ERL1-FLAG protein with at least three different sizes, suggestive of heterogeneous glycans (Figure 7D, blue and cyan arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D and by inference about glycan heterogeneity.

claim: ERL1-FLAG protein from Stomagen-treated seedlings was hypersensitive to Endo-H and cleaved completely.
source: In contrast, ERL1-FLAG protein from Stomagen-treated seedlings was hypersensitive to Endo-H and cleaved completely (Figure 7D, light arrow).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The tmm mutation enhanced the Endo-H sensitivity of ERL1.
source: Likewise, the tmm mutation enhanced the Endo-H sensitivity of ERL1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), suggesting an increase in endoplasmic reticulum retention.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The tmm mutation suggests an increase in endoplasmic reticulum retention of ERL1.
source: Likewise, the tmm mutation enhanced the Endo-H sensitivity of ERL1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), suggesting an increase in endoplasmic reticulum retention.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the increased Endo-H sensitivity of ERL1 in tmm mutants.

claim: Exogenous application of Stomagen blocks the activation of ERECTA-family signaling.
source: Because exogenous application of Stomagen blocks the activation of ERECTA-family signaling (Lee et al., 2015) and results in stomatal clustering (Figure 7A)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2015 and by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Exogenous application of Stomagen results in stomatal clustering.
source: Because exogenous application of Stomagen blocks the activation of ERECTA-family signaling (Lee et al., 2015) and results in stomatal clustering (Figure 7A)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Tyr A23 treatment enhanced ERL1-YFP signals in the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: Indeed, the Tyr A23 treatment enhanced ERL1-YFP signals in the endoplasmic reticulum (Figure 7E, pink arrow), whereas in mock ERL1-YFP was only detected on the plasma membrane and endosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Tyr A23 is an inhibitor that has been widely used to block clathrin-mediated endocytosis in plant cells.
source: For this purpose, we first treated erecta erl1 erl2 seedlings expressing ERL1-YFP with Tyr A23, an inhibitor that has been widely used to block clathrin-mediated endocytosis in plant cells (Banbury et al., 2003; Santuari et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Banbury et al., 2003 and Santuari et al., 2011, and by established knowledge about Tyr A23.

claim: Tyr A23 functions as a protonophore, which inadvertently blocks endocytosis through cytoplasmic acidification.
source: A recent report showed that Tyr A23 functions as a protonophore, which inadvertently blocks endocytosis through cytoplasmic acidification (Dejonghe et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Dejonghe et al., 2016.

claim: ES9-17 is a specific inhibitor of clathrin-mediated endocytosis without the side effects of cytoplasmic acidification.
source: Chemical screening and subsequent derivatization identified ES9-17 as a specific inhibitor of clathrin-mediated endocytosis without the side effects of cytoplasmic acidification (Dejonghe et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Dejonghe et al., 2019.

claim: At 100 μM, ES9-17 inhibited the internalization of FM4-64 dye in epidermal pavement cells and stomatal-lineage cells.
source: At 100 μM, ES9-17 inhibited the internalization of FM4-64 dye in epidermal pavement cells and stomatal-lineage cells, just like 50 μM ES9-17 in root cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3A and 3B.

claim: ES9-17 treatment caused the accumulation of ERL1-YFP in the endoplasmic reticulum, just like the Tyr A23 treatment.
source: Under this condition, ES9-17 treatment caused the accumulation of ERL1-YFP in the endoplasmic reticulum, just like the Tyr A23 treatment (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Inefficient endocytosis due to perception of an antagonistic peptide, Stomagen, causes retention of ERL1-YFP in the endoplasmic reticulum.

claim: The cytoplasmic domain of ERL1 is critical for its proper subcellular dynamics.

claim: Both EPF1 and EPFL6 peptides trigger ERL1 endocytosis.
